A useful map of the mind

In my guides when I refer to your ‘subconscious’ I am referring to everything going on beneath the surface of your conscious mind – perceptions, emotions, desires, aversions, imagery, memories, body signals, habits, intuitions, automatic behaviours etc. Sometimes it is useful to work with all of these as one ‘mind’, other times it can be more effective to work with the ‘ecology’ of parts. Neither way is ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ it is just a question of using the right map for the job in hand.

Working with parts is about precision, working with the Higher Self is about coherence – you need to move in and out of communion with both.

To work with the ‘whole’ – the subconscious as one:

“Invoke” the subconscious – e.g. ‘Hello wise subconscious can you help me understand…..’

To work with ‘parts’ recognise the ‘ecology’ in the subconscious – there may be a child part that wants love, a protector part that wants to keep you safe, a ‘critic’ that wants you to live up to certain standards, a fantasy making part, body memory parts, a social part, a spiritual part that wants to connect to God/source/do what is in the best benefit of all beings, a ‘wiser’ part etc etc

Generally it is a good idea to start with unity:

“Invoke” your Higher Self – e.g. ‘Hello my Higher Self/universal heart-mind/wise subconscious please can you help me…..’

Then move into differentiation if needed:

Ask “Which part is afraid? Which part is protecting? Which part is avoiding? Which part knows what to do? Which part is too young for this?”

Then move back into unity – recognising that it is all part of the same life and ideally all parts should be led by the ‘adult’ self operating from a place of love.

Sometimes start with the whole

For some people, it is better not to start by asking for the 12 parts, or by giving everybody an office. For these people, it is better to start from the Sacred whole.

In order to do this, I start with a prayer: ‘Let’s begin by connecting to the universal heart (or to my Higher Self). The universal heart (or the Higher Self) is the part of me that existed before I was born and that will exist after I am gone. It is the part of me that is not wounded, the part of me that is not caught in any roles, or families or groups. The part of me that has no identities, no ideologies, and no stories. From this place, let’s ask for what is true, kind, timely, stabilizing and useful.’

Sometimes, people don’t have access to their Higher Self, or to the universal heart, or whatever language you might use that feels sacred for you. In that case, I’ll just begin by asking them to start witnessing, to notice things around them, or in their body, or to notice that they are in a younger state. The fact that they can notice is usually enough of an adult function to begin with.

Once people can notice, and distinguish, there’s no point in working more on their Witness. Begin working on whatever else they need: warmth, protection, direction etc. So while the language of the Higher Self is useful in order to bring people together, it doesn’t mean that all the adult functions are already there. You’ll need to work on growing them.

It is important to differentiate but only as needed when something comes up. “Is this coming from my inner child? Is it a protector? Is this my body speaking? Is this fear speaking? Is this intuition? Is this social conditioning speaking? Is this divine guidance or my interpretation of guidance?”

But always start from the heart, differentiate as needed, and then come back to the heart.

Appendix C: The extended de-hypnosis checklist

Things to Consider When Influence is Occurring

Take a Time Out and say to yourself:

I see that influence is occurring. I don’t have to act on it. I don’t have to attack it. I can take a time out. I can consider what is being presupposed here. I can consider who benefits here. I can pay attention to what my body is telling me, without believing it tells the whole story. I can ask some questions, such as how does this square with love? How does this square with truth? How does this square with humility? How does this fit with ordinary life?

Then say to yourself: If it’s true, it will survive the passage of time. If it’s love, it will survive the passage of time. If it’s what I’m supposed to do, it will survive the passage of time. If it’s really for me, it will survive my being an adult.

Then ask yourself: Is there any …

sense of urgency? sense of secrecy? sense of shame? threatening to not include me if I don’t do what I’m being influenced to do? promise of specialness? sexual charge? sense of spiritual superiority? direct request for money, sex, loyalty, silence, or obedience? way in which my choices are being narrowed? way in which questioning is being equated with betrayal? way in which my resistance is being pathologized? way in which ordinary life is being downgraded?

Who are you allowing to seduce, scare, or rescue your child?

Are you allowing them to remove your ability to say NO?

If yes to any of these, but especially if yes to more than one, you need to stop going deeper into trance or making decisions you can’t reverse, and come back into your room, your body, your food, your sleep, your time, and your counsel.

Good guides increase your adult self; bad guides replace it. Good guides are fine with you saying NO; bad guides frame your NO as resistance, your ego, fear, low vibration, trauma, sin, and evidence that you need more of their guidance.

Hypnosis-specific audit

Before listening to a recording or before going into a live situation, make sure that the answer to each of the following questions is yes. If not, become fully alert, modify, or stop:

Were induction mechanics plainly explained to me?

Can my answers allow me to become fully alert, modify, or stop the process?

Is it hidden in a secret that not noticing is a proof of process?

Is a role or ownership, obedience, age, identity, or belonging being used to make me less responsible and to remove my adult judgment from the process?

Were fractionation, cues, later behavior, and memory effects plainly explained to me before the process?

Were somatic argumentation mechanics plainly explained to me?

Will the exit process restore me to my normal identity, movement, orientation, and critical judgment, and state plainly that the process is over?

If in doubt, become fully alert, ask to see the script, modify, or leave the process.

Appendix D: Anxiety — body first

Remember that the anxiety is coming from a part of yourself that is a Protector who believes they are trying to save yourself from something bad happening. Maybe they are trying to protect yourself from danger, shame, abandonment, failure, exposure, illness, rejection, losing control, or something that the protector believes will be unbearable for yourself. Rather than getting into a dialogue where it feels as though yourself is interrogating the protector, start with yourself by taking care of the body.

Always work with yourself by taking care of the body first, then the inner child, then doing some inner inquiry work, and then taking some kind of action.

Inner child love

One of the things that can help is putting your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexis and say lovingly, “You are a little one. You are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. Let the adult take this.”

Don’t say the words, just hoping that they will work on your subconscious mind. Say them to yourself like you are talking to a little child that you love.

Reduced breathing / Buteyko-style breathing

NOTE: There are some good things to be said for slowing down the breathing, especially for overbreathers and those subject to panic. Some of this is based on the Buteyko approach. However, it should not be forced, and creating air hunger can increase anxiety for a short period. Take things slowly.

Try breathing through the nose. Try small inhales. Try quiet exhales. Try pausing if it is comfortable. See if it is possible to quiet the breathing. STOP if this creates dizziness, strain, a sense of panic or any other medical concerns.

EFT tapping

One of the simplest aspects of EFT is that it’s something you can do in your body. If you’re worried about something, you can name it, tap on your body, and get in touch with the feeling. There isn’t a ton of evidence, but a 2025 systematic review of EFT and anxiety disorders found seven randomized control trials and noted that EFT was more effective than no intervention in several studies. While it should be handled with a bit of caution, it’s something to keep in mind if you’re not responding to first-line therapies.

Even though I have this anxiety, I am willing to be kind to myself.

Somatic Experiencing

Try out a word or phrase to see if it fits, but also look at what it says about the situation. A word that feels ok might say something that doesn’t fit. It’s good to use both to correct each other.

Body supports

Sometimes the mind is too activated to let meditation to take care of it. It may be useful to start from the body instead. Consider massage, either self or given by someone else, as the first resort. Maybe massage the top of one foot with the other, or the scalp, or a temple, or the back of the neck, or the top of a shoulder, or whatever feels good to touch. (Avoid the front of the neck. Avoid injured, numb, bruised, inflamed, recently surgically-operated-on areas, and varicose veins. Stop if it makes the anxiety symptoms or anything else feel bad, whether immediately or later, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) Other body approaches that may help include heat, pressure, weighted blanket, darkness, favorite calming music, massage gun, etc.

Others mentioned warmth, darkness, favorite music, massage, weighted blanket, breathwork, favorite object, and favorite personal technology.

Anxiety script

I will re-inhabit my body: first my feet, and my chair, and my breath, and the room around me.

When this is done, if there is a little person, I will reassure him: "It's okay, you're safe now, I'm here. Thank you, protector, for alerting me; you don't have to scream, I can hear you."

Then I will see if there is anything I need to do. If there is, I'll just pick the first little thing to do, and do that. If there's nothing I need to do, I'll see if I can help my body stand down.

Either way, I don't abandon the signal, or worship it -- I'll do something.
